chain.label: Mountainous terrain surrounding Aspen airport
chain.trigger: surrounded on all sides by high terrain

chain.label: Mountain shadow caused darkness well before official night
chain.trigger: the sun had set below the mountainous terrain about 25 minutes before the official sunset time...evening civil twilight ended about 1830 rather than 1855

caused_by.evidence: the mountainous terrain surrounding ASE reduces the amount of ambient lighting during evening civil twilight at lower elevations

chain.label: Deteriorating visibility and light snow near ASE
chain.trigger: the visibility north of the airport was 2 miles

chain.label: Crew planned a single visual approach attempt under time/fuel pressure
chain.trigger: we're not going to have a bunch of extra gas so we only get to shoot it once and then we're going to Rifle

chain.label: Captain's approach briefing omitted instrument and missed-approach procedures
chain.trigger: the CVR indicated that the captain did not discuss the instrument approach procedure during his approach briefing...the captain also did not brief the missed approach procedure

caused_by.evidence: the captain did not discuss the instrument approach procedure...because he expected to execute a visual approach to the airport

chain.label: Crew omitted required approach callouts and did not challenge the captain
chain.trigger: the CVR did not record any of these callouts...the first officer did not challenge the captain's actions

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew was not adequately prepared to perform ASE's instrument and missed approach procedures

chain.label: Captain deployed spoilers with gear/flaps extended and reduced power below minimum
chain.trigger: the captain deployed the spoilers after the landing gear had been extended and the final landing flaps had been selected...engine power was set to 55 percent N2

caused_by.evidence: the captain likely extended the spoilers and reduced engine power to increase the airplane's rate of descent to get below the snow showers and visually acquire the runway

chain.label: Airplane descended below step-down altitudes and the MDA without visual contact with the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane was now operating below the 10,200-foot MDA without any indication...that either pilot had made visual contact with the runway or its environment

caused_by.evidence: the captain continued flight below the authorized MDA after failing to establish or maintain visual contact with the runway
the first officer did not verbally challenge the captain, and radar data showed that the captain did not correct the descent or initiate a missed approach

chain.label: Crew never clearly established, or lost, visual contact with the runway
chain.trigger: the captain's statement 'where's it at?' indicated that he did not see any of these visual references

caused_by.evidence: the dark conditions would have significantly degraded the flight crew's ability to see and safely avoid terrain
the reduced visibility and light snow showers near the airport would have further degraded the flight crew's ability to see and safely avoid the terrain

chain.label: Captain continued the approach instead of executing a missed approach
chain.trigger: at this point, the captain should have abandoned the approach, especially because the airplane was close to the ground in mountainous terrain

caused_by.evidence: the flight crewmembers should have abandoned the approach because the airplane descended below the MDA without an adequate visual reference of the runway
the captain, as the flying pilot, should not have been relying on the first officer for directional guidance during the visual transition from the instrument approach to the landing

chain.label: Airplane entered a steep, uncontrolled left bank close to terrain
chain.trigger: the GPWS bank angle alert when the airplane was banked about 40º left wing down

caused_by.evidence: the airplane stopped turning to the right and began turning to the left...the airplane's bank angle continued to increase

these actions were contrary to spoiler information in the Gulfstream GIII Flight Manual...the high-pressure rpm power setting...should not be below 64 percent N2 to meet FAA-required go-around standards

chain.label: Airplane struck sloping terrain short of the runway
chain.trigger: the airplane crashed into terrain while in a steep left bank about 2,400 feet short of the runway 15 threshold

caused_by.evidence: the airplane crashed into terrain while in a steep left bank

chain.label: All occupants killed
chain.trigger: All of the passengers and crewmembers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: All of the passengers and crewmembers were killed
